claim_checks.claim: It removed the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions ✅[3]
claim_checks.page_says: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport. ... Make MCP stateless: remove the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake.
claim_checks.note: Changelog lists both removals as major changes since 2025-11-25. Summary claim mapped to role 3 (the lifecycle sections it summarizes).

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.5 Current lifecycle (2026-07-28): no handshake
claim_checks.claim: A request missing a required key is rejected with `-32602`, and with HTTP 400 on HTTP ✅[7]
claim_checks.page_says: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: MUST on both parts; matches the plain statement.

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.5 Current lifecycle (2026-07-28): no handshake
claim_checks.claim: On HTTP there is nothing to shut down: each request is its own POST ✅[13]
claim_checks.page_says: Each request is its own POST ... servers could assign a session via the Mcp-Session-Id header (terminated with HTTP DELETE) ... None of these mechanisms are part of this revision.
claim_checks.note: The only HTTP teardown mechanism (session DELETE) is stated as absent from 2026-07-28; DELETE gets 405 per the same page.

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.6 End-to-end session in six steps
claim_checks.claim: `notifications/tools/list_changed`, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection ✅[4][13] (Legacy 2025-11-25 column)
claim_checks.page_says: [4] lifecycle: "listChanged: Support for list change notifications (for prompts, resources, and tools)"; [4] transports: "The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream."
claim_checks.note: Searched 'list_changed' in both [4] pages: not found. The cell is labelled 2025-11-25 by its column, so [13] (a 2026-07-28 page, which names the method only for the subscriptions/listen stream) cannot supply the legacy method name. The GET-stream delivery part is supported; the method name for the legacy era is not. The name does appear in the uncited 2025-11-25 security page ([4a-sess]), so this is true per an uncited cached page.

claim_checks.section: ## 2. Q2: Primitives > ### 2.1 Server primitives (who controls them)
claim_checks.claim: A missing resource is error `-32602` in 2026-07-28 (it was `-32002` before; clients should still accept `-32002`) ✅[17][3]
claim_checks.page_says: servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (Invalid Params). ... clients SHOULD also accept -32002 as a resource not found error, as earlier protocol versions used this code
claim_checks.note: [3] also: 'Change resource not found error code from -32002 to -32602'.

claim_checks.claim: The client gathers the input and retries the original request with a new `id`, `inputResponses` and the echoed `requestState` ✅[23]
claim_checks.page_says: the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request ... The JSON-RPC id MUST be different between the initial request and the retry
claim_checks.note: The preceding sentence marks requestState as optional, which matches the page's 'If an InputRequiredResult contains the requestState field' condition.

claim_checks.claim: Worked example (2026-07-28, from the spec): `tools/call` id 2 returns an `input_required` result asking for a GitHub username via form elicitation; the client retries `tools/call` as id 3 with `inputResponses: {"github_login":{"action":"accept","content":{"name":"octocat"}}}` and the same `requestState` ✅[14][23]
claim_checks.note: [14] example matches ids 2 and 3, form mode, github_login key, accept action, octocat, and the same requestState value on retry.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.1 The standard transports
claim_checks.claim: optional `MCP-Session-Id`; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client `DELETE` to end ✅[4] (2025-11-25 column, Sessions row)
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request. ... Clients ... SHOULD send an HTTP DELETE
claim_checks.note: '400 without it' and 'client DELETE to end' are SHOULD rules written as plain statements; the 400 also drops the condition 'servers that require a session ID', and the DELETE drops that the server MAY answer 405. The 404 part is MUST and is fine.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.4 Choosing a transport
claim_checks.claim: keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP ✅[13]
claim_checks.page_says: Servers wanting to support older clients should: Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint”
claim_checks.note: Decision-table advice; matches the page's backward-compatibility guidance.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.4 Choosing a transport
claim_checks.page_says: [15]: "It replaces the former resources/subscribe RPC and the HTTP GET endpoint." [4]: "The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream."
claim_checks.note: Each era checked against its own page: [15] lists toolsListChanged; [4] lifecycle ties listChanged to tool list change notifications and [4] transports lets the GET stream carry notifications.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.5 Authorization for HTTP servers (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: Dropped qualifier: the page says 'security best practices', the claim says 'best practice' (wider scope). Modal MUST matches.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.5 Authorization for HTTP servers (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. ... with insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: ... HTTP 403 Forbidden status code
claim_checks.note: Token validation, audience check and 401 are MUST and are fine. The 403/insufficient_scope/scope clause sits under the item's leading 'must' (and the list is introduced as normative), but the page says SHOULD: a modal raised to MUST level.

claim_checks.section: ## 4. Q4: Security and trust > ### 4.2 Requirements by actor (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Resources ✅[17]: servers must validate URIs and sanitize `file://` paths against traversal.
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate all resource URIs ... Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving file:// resources
claim_checks.note: The mark sits after the label; grounded the rule it labels.

claim_checks.section: ## 4. Q4: Security and trust > ### 4.4 Confused deputy
claim_checks.claim: SSRF through metadata URLs (clients should require HTTPS and block private ranges, and use an egress proxy on servers) ✅[30] (under 'Related attacks with required mitigations')
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients SHOULD require HTTPS for all OAuth-related URLs in production environments ... For server-side MCP client deployments, operators SHOULD consider using an egress proxy
claim_checks.note: Dropped condition 'in production environments' on HTTPS; 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' written as 'should use'. Private-range blocking (SHOULD) matches. The clause carries its own 'should', so the lead-in 'required mitigations' is not treated as a MUST raise, but it misleads: the page's only MUST here is that clients deployed to a server 'MUST consider SSRF risks and implement appropriate mitigations'.

violations.evidence: S4: legacy column names `notifications/tools/list_changed` citing [4][13]; neither 2025-11-25 page in [4] contains the name, and [13] is a 2026-07-28 page.
S12: step 9 puts the 403 insufficient_scope response under a leading 'must'; [26] says the server SHOULD respond with 403.
S8: Sessions row (2025-11-25) states '400 without it' and 'client DELETE to end' plainly; [4] has SHOULD for both and limits the 400 to servers that require a session ID.
S11: 'established best practice' drops the qualifier 'security' from [26]'s 'established security best practices'.
S14: SSRF mitigations drop 'in production environments' for HTTPS and turn 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' into 'use an egress proxy' ([30]).
